source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_76/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Perform the join on 'city' as specified
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="city", how="inner")

# Select only the columns required by the target schema
# Target schema: ['city': string, 'fare': float, 'ride_id': integer]
# Convert 'ride_id' to integer (it may be large, so use int64)
result = joined[['city', 'fare', 'ride_id']].copy()
result['fare'] = result['fare'].astype(float)
result['ride_id'] = result['ride_id'].astype('int64')

# Write the result to the specified path without the index
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_76/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_76/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_76/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on 'city'
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="city", how="inner")

# Group by 'city' (primary key), aggregate fare by average, ride_id by max (to keep integer type and consistent with examples)
result = joined.groupby("city", as_index=False).agg({
    "fare": "mean",
    "ride_id": "max"
})

# Ensure column order and names exactly as target schema
result = result[["city", "fare", "ride_id"]]

# Write output
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_76/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
